newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan closes down at one-month low vs US dollar.
newsitem.headline: Yuan closes down at one-month low vs US dollar.

text.p: The Chinese yuan on Tuesday closed down at a one-month low of 8.2955 from Monday's 8.2945 against the U.S. dollar in Shanghai because of intervention from the central bank, dealers said.

Trading started at 09:20 a.m. (0120 GMT) as usual but was suspended for one hour from 10:00 a.m. (0200 GMT) due to Deng Xiaoping's funeral. The one-hour loss was compensated for by extra trading from 11:00 to 12:00 a.m (0300 to 0400 GMT).
The funeral started at 10:00 a.m. (0200 GMT) on Tuesday and lasted for nearly one hour.
The weighted average price on Monday was 8.2938.
Dealers said the People's Bank of China was seen depressing the yuan late in trading to weaken pro-yuan sentiment.
The yuan opened up at 8.2939 and consolidated around the 8.2940 level early in the session, hitting an intraday high of 8.2935 before trading was suspended.
The yuan moved in a wide range after trading resumed, hitting a low of 8.2990 five minutes before the close.
Trading was active early but turned dull late in trading, with most done at the 8.2950 level, dealers said.
"Intervention from the central bank decided the market direction," said one dealer. "The intervention will hurt pro-yuan market sentiment and result in more selling of yuan into the market."
Dealers said the yuan was seen likely to touch the main support 8.30 level in the short term.
They said they expected the yuan to move around the 8.2950 level on Wednesday.
The yuan continued its fall to close lower at 6.7810 from 6.7635 against 100 Japanese yen and unchanged at 1.0720 against the Hong Kong dollar.
